questions.q: What does the Debug panel actually run when you click Run?
options: A simulated, non-functional preview of the flow
Only the Decision elements in the flow
The last activated version of the flow, regardless of unsaved edits
The flow's most recently saved version, executed for real with the sample input you provide
questions.explain: Debug executes the most recently saved version of the flow for real, using the input values you enter, and traces what happens.

questions.q: Why would debugging a flow 'as yourself' miss a problem that a real user hits?
options: You are almost always a System Administrator with fewer sharing restrictions than the actual user
Debug never uses real data
Debug always runs in rollback mode automatically
The Debug panel cannot access record data at all
questions.explain: Admin users typically bypass sharing and field-level restrictions that a lower-access user would hit — 'Run automation as another user' reproduces the real experience.

questions.q: In the lesson's debug example, what did the Debug Details panel show when 'Close Tasks' failed?
options: A governor limit exceeded error
A syntax error in a formula field
INSUFFICIENT_ACCESS_ON_CROSS_REFERENCE_ENTITY, with the exact filter and field values the element used
An email deliverability failure
questions.explain: The Debug Details panel showed the real platform error — insufficient access on the referenced object — plus the exact query and update details.

questions.q: What makes Flow Test different from a one-off Debug run?
options: Flow Test only works on screen flows
Flow Test cannot check record data, only UI elements
Flow Test replaces the need for a fault path
Flow Test is saved and can be re-run on demand, including after future edits to the flow
questions.explain: A Flow Test saves a triggering record and assertions permanently, so it can be re-run any time — proving the flow still behaves correctly after later changes.

questions.q: What does 'Run automation in rollback mode' do during a debug run?
options: It deactivates the flow after the run completes
It executes the flow for real but prevents the changes from actually being saved
It skips all fault paths during the run
It reverts the flow to its previous saved version
questions.explain: Rollback mode lets you observe a real execution and its results without the data changes actually persisting in the org.
